newsitem.title: USA: Banned oxygen generators shipped on Continental jet.
newsitem.headline: Banned oxygen generators shipped on Continental jet.

text.p: The U.S. Federal Aviation Administration has opened an investigation into a shipment of banned oxygen generators on a Continental Airlines flight from Los Angeles to Houston in April, the airline said Tuesday.

The generators, similar to ones believed to have ignited a fire that downed ValuJet Flight 592 last May, were mistakenly stowed aboard a Continental flight between Los Angeles and Houston on April 16, the airline said in a statement.
"The oxygen generators were shipped as cargo by a vendor who did not disclose that they were hazardous materials," the Houston-based carrier said.

Continental said it notified the FAA on April 25 that the seven disarmed and capped generators were mistakenly shipped as cargo on the flight. The airline is working with the agency to determine how the generators were placed on its plane.
"The airline immediately reported this occurrence to the FAA when the shipment was discovered," the airline said.

Packed in boxes labeled "airline parts," the generators had been taken off Continental planes and were being shipped back to the airline's facilities in Houston by a vendor, spokeswoman Karla Villalon said.

Shipments of oxygen generators were banned on commercial airliners after the ValuJet crash in the Florida Everglades that killed all 110 people on board. Preliminary reports indicated the crash was caused by a fire in the cargo hold ignited by mislabeled and improperly stored oxygen canisters.
